implementation_notes: Qt ships the role set: QMdiArea is the view handler for multi-document layouts - subWindowList() enumerates the open views, tileSubWindows()/cascadeSubWindows()/closeAllSubWindows() are the meta-commands, and each QMdiSubWindow is re-parented so destruction is automatic; for one-view-at-a-time shells QStackedWidget switches with setCurrentIndex()/setCurrentWidget() while keeping every page alive. The factory half is a registry of QObject-creating callables (QHash<QString, std::function<QWidget*(Model*)>>) or Qt's plugin mechanism, and change propagation is a model signal connected to a slot that calls update() on the affected widgets. What remains the application's job is the dependency knowledge - which view shows which part of the model - because Qt coordinates windows, not semantics.
pitfalls: QMdiArea owns every subwindow: a view that must outlive the area has to be removed with removeSubWindow() and re-parented, otherwise Qt deletes it with the area.
Iterating subWindowList() while a slot opens or closes a subwindow (activation signals fire during close) mutates the list mid-iteration - collect the handles first.
QStackedWidget keeps all pages constructed but hidden pages receive no resize/show events, so state that depends on them must be refreshed explicitly when the page is switched in.
Connections to a destroyed widget are only safe when the sender outlives it; prefer the receiver-context overload connect(sender, signal, context, slot) so a closed view cannot be invoked.

variants.name: MFC document/view with CDocTemplate (classic Windows)
variants.implementation_notes: The classic Windows realization: CDocTemplate instances registered with the application create documents and their frame+view pairs on demand, CFrameWnd owns the view inside the frame, and the MDI frame window implements the view meta-commands (MDITile, MDICascade, MDIIconArrange), while the document keeps the list of views opened on it. The registry of open views therefore lives in the document and the frame objects rather than in a class you write, and creating a second view of a document is CDocTemplate::CreateNewFrame(doc, otherView). Choose this variant in existing MFC codebases; it is Windows-only and its lifecycle hooks (OnCreate/OnClose/PostNcDestroy) fire in framework-defined order.
pitfalls: MFC creates views through CDocTemplate, never with new: constructing a view directly bypasses the document/frame wiring and yields a view with no document.
The framework owns lifetime - OnClose and PostNcDestroy delete the view - so a hand-maintained pointer registry must remove its entry in OnDestroy or it dangles.
Reusing one document across MDI children leaks per-document state when a second view mutates shared data; the model belongs to the document, not to the view.
